blocks.text: Documents why web_researcher.py and similar agents need a pre-filter, and traces the history from the original Groq llama-prompt-guard-2-86m (which silently failed on every real input due to context-window math) to the current local Laya forward pass.
blocks.title: Module header: why this exists and the Laya migration

blocks.text: CLASSIFICATION_QUESTION defines the three-way Laya choice task. _FLAG_ONLY controls whether flagged snippets are dropped or annotated. _CHUNK_CHARS (1000) and _MAX_CHUNKS_PER_SNIPPET (5) are sized to fit Laya's context and cap per-snippet cost; comments explain the token math behind both values.
blocks.title: Module-level constants and configuration

blocks.text: _classify_chunk makes one Laya predict call and extracts the uppercased label from the response. Any error (None result, KeyError, TypeError) degrades to an empty string — the caller (score_snippet) catches Exception as an additional layer, but _classify_chunk itself never propagates.
blocks.title: Single-chunk classifier

blocks.text: Splits text into chunks, calls _classify_chunk on each (up to _MAX_CHUNKS_PER_SNIPPET), and returns {flagged: True, reason: label} at the first INJECTION or JAILBREAK result. Classification failures are printed and treated as not-flagged. Empty/whitespace-only text is fast-pathed to {flagged: False}.
blocks.title: Snippet scorer

blocks.text: Iterates over a list of dicts, calls score_snippet on each item's text field, and applies the _FLAG_ONLY policy: annotate-and-keep when True, drop silently when False. Scoring failures on one item do not stop the rest of the batch.
blocks.title: Batch filter for snippet lists

gotchas: _FLAG_ONLY=True means flagged snippets are kept with a marker, not dropped — callers must check _injection_flagged themselves if they want to exclude flagged content
Chunks over ~300 tokens are silently truncated by Laya's context window; _CHUNK_CHARS=1000 is sized to stay under that limit for typical prose
The classifier screens only the first 5 chunks of any one snippet — a very long injected instruction buried deep in the text may not be caught
how_it_works: CLASSIFICATION_QUESTION defines a three-way Laya choice task (benign/injection/jailbreak) used by _classify_chunk
_classify_chunk calls laya_gate.predict with the chunk and returns the uppercased label string; any error degrades to empty string

score_snippet splits text into _CHUNK_CHARS-sized chunks (1000 chars), screens up to _MAX_CHUNKS_PER_SNIPPET (5), and returns {flagged, reason}; any INJECTION or JAILBREAK label flags the whole snippet
filter_snippets maps score_snippet over a list of dicts; when _FLAG_ONLY=True (the default) flagged items are kept with a _injection_flagged:True marker; when False they are dropped entirely
inputs: raw text string from scraped sources
list of snippet dicts with configurable text and label keys
purpose: Acts as a defense-in-depth pre-filter for text pulled from the open web by agents such as web_researcher.py and part_price_finder.py. Splits long text into chunks and runs each through a local Laya forward pass that classifies it as benign, injection, or jailbreak. The module is fail-open: any classifier error is logged and treated as not-flagged to avoid blocking real product data lookups.
side_effects: Laya local forward pass (CPU inference, no network) per chunk
print() to stdout for flagged snippets and classification failures
